blocks.text: Exercises: sentences and translations from Tatoeba (tatoeba.org, CC BY 2.0 FR).

exercises.prompt: Mary is a professional pole dancer.
exercises.why: The genitive case of Russian nouns is more frequently used and has many more functions than any other case in the Russian language. The genitive case is used to denote the possessor or owner which in English is rendered by the ending -'s (-s') or by the construction with the preposition of: *Книга студента.* — The student's book. *Автомобиль учителя.* — The teacher's car. The genitive denoting the possessor or owner answers the question чей? (чья? чьё? чьи?) — whose? *Чей это автомобиль? — Это автомобиль учителя. A noun in the genitive case is sometimes used to qualify (modify) another noun. It answers then the question какой?: *здание почты* — the post office building; *улицы города* — the… — DLI, Lessons 23, 24, 27 and 33.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: The genitive case of Russian nouns is more frequently used and has many more functions than any other case in the Russian language. (DLI, Lessons 23, 24, 27 and 33)
